items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: read Vortex's DB so Workshop collections with no local collection.json show up, then let the user pull it from Nexus
items.why: Missing Files' own picker only reads local staging folders, so a Workshop collection with no collection.json on disk is invisible to it — Rebuild Collection solves this the same way (reads the needed data, including the Nexus slug, straight from Vortex's DB) and then offers a Nexus pull. Bring the same two-part fix here.
items.prompt:
Real feature, director's own hypothesis: the mass 'archive mismatch' results in Rebuild Missing Files may be caused by a STALE local `collection.json` (not updated to match what's published on Nexus), the same class of staleness Rebuild Collection already has a manual fix for.

GROUNDING (read before writing anything, don't reinvent):
- The reusable pull-fresh-collection.json function already exists: `fetchAndExtractCollectionJson({ slug, revisionNumber, destDir, sevenZipExe })` in `lib/nexus-collection-download.js:219` — fetches Nexus's v2 GraphQL collection-revision API, resolves a signed CDN download URL, downloads the collection's `.7z` bundle, extracts just `collection.json` into `destDir`.
- Today it's wired as a MANUAL button on Rebuild Collection — `POST /workshop/fetch-from-nexus` (`web/rebuild-routes.js:180`), not an automatic step before every run. Match that same 'manual, explicit action' shape here rather than silently auto-refreshing on every scan (a network call + overwrite shouldn't happen without the user asking for it).
- **IMPORTANT NUANCE, correct scoping needed**: this only ever fetches the collection's last PUBLISHED revision from Nexus. For a Workshop-authored (in-progress) collection, this can genuinely be STALE relative to the user's own local, not-yet-published edits — it is NOT simply 'the latest,' despite the director's own framing. Don't silently apply this to Workshop collections as if it were a strict improvement; surface this distinction in the UI copy itself (something like 'Pulls the last version you published to Nexus — won't include any local changes you haven't uploaded yet' for Workshop rows specifically) so the director isn't surprised if it overwrites in-progress local authoring work with an older published state.
- **Destructive today, no backup** — `extractFile`'s own `7z e ... -y` silently overwrites `collection.json` with zero backup of the prior file (`lib/sevenzip.js:100`). GENUINE IMPROVEMENT to make here, not just a straight port: back up the existing `collection.json` (copy it alongside with a timestamp suffix, or into this app's own established backup convention if one exists for small config-like files — check how Update Collection's own 'Create Backup' step names/stores its backups and mirror that pattern if it fits) before overwriting, so a bad/unwanted refresh is recoverable.
- **Slug resolution gap**: `lib/missing-files-scan.js`'s `listPickableCollections` (line 60) reads purely from local staging folders — it has NO Nexus slug for any collection today (unlike Rebuild Collection, which gets `collectionSlug` from Vortex's own live state cache). Need to add a way to resolve each pickable collection's own Nexus slug — check whether `collection.json` itself already records its own slug/id (likely, under `info` or similar — inspect a real one) before assuming a live Vortex-state read is required; prefer reading it straight from the collection.json already on disk if the field exists, since that avoids a Vortex-state dependency this tool has deliberately avoided so far (`listPickableCollections`' own header comment: 'no Vortex live-state read at all').

SCOPE: add a small 'Refresh from Nexus' action per collection card on the Step 1 picker (`design/vortex-rebuild-missing-files-mockup.html`'s own picker screen, or wherever fits without breaking the existing approved layout — flag if this needs its own small mockup addendum rather than guessing the placement). Clicking it: backs up the current collection.json, calls `fetchAndExtractCollectionJson`, shows success/failure, and — for a Workshop row specifically — shows the local-edits-may-be-lost caveat BEFORE proceeding (a confirm step, not just inline copy, given it's a real overwrite risk).

VOICE: run new copy through plain-language-writer. This is a real 'writes to a file that represents meaningful local state, possibly overwriting in-progress work' action — serious register for the confirm/caveat text, matching this app's own established registry for consequential actions.

VERIFY: real test against a genuinely stale collection (deliberately don't refresh one for a bit if needed, or use one already confirmed stale from the earlier archive-mismatch investigation) — confirm refreshing actually reduces/resolves the false 'archive mismatch' count for that collection afterward, and confirm the backup file is real and restorable. Handoff with what you tested and the real before/after mismatch counts if you can get them.

SEQUENCING (director's own call): build the pull mechanism FIRST, verified working, before touching any warning copy. Once the pull itself is confirmed solid, add the SAME 'before fetching, read this' warning Rebuild Collection already shows for Workshop collections — reuse it verbatim, don't rewrite it:
  "⚠️ Before fetching, read this
  1. This only fetches a revision already saved to NexusMods (published or not) — pick the one you want from the Revision dropdown below.
  2. If you've made changes in the Workshop since your last save/upload, this download will not include them.
  3. Recommended: save/upload your latest Workshop changes to NexusMods first, then fetch here.
  4. If you skip that, you'll need to manually reconcile any unsaved changes yourself after rebuilding."
(source: `web/public/index.html` lines 273-281, `#workshopOnlySection`'s own callout--warning). Reuse the identical markup/classes too (`callout callout--warning`, nested callout, `<ol>`), matching DESIGN.md's 'copy an existing report's markup, don't design from a blank page' rule — this is the same warning in a new spot, not a new pattern.

SCOPE CORRECTION FROM THE DIRECTOR (important, changes root cause): this isn't just about a STALE collection.json — some Workshop collections have NO collection.json on disk at all, so `listPickableCollections` (which only scans local staging folders) never sees them in the first place. Rebuild Collection already solves exactly this: it reads Vortex's own database directly to discover these 'Workshop-only' collections (name, modId, and critically the Nexus `collectionSlug`, since the slug itself isn't recoverable from anywhere on disk if there's no collection.json) — see `lib/collection-runner.js`'s `loadSyncStateBatch` and `web/rebuild-routes.js`'s `/vortex-data/refresh` (~line 24, 41-58, 292-305), which populates `workshopOnlyCollections` and caches it in `vortexDataSession`/`syncStateCache`, then `/collections` (~line 127-167) merges that into what the picker shows, each entry carrying `collectionSlug` (from the cached sync-state's `data.collectionSlug`, ~line 143).

REVISED SCOPE:
1. `lib/missing-files-scan.js`'s `listPickableCollections` needs a Vortex-DB read added, mirroring Rebuild Collection's own `/vortex-data/refresh` flow — reuse `collection-runner.js`'s `loadSyncStateBatch`/whatever the exact shared primitive is, don't reimplement Vortex-DB reading from scratch. This surfaces Workshop-only collections (no local collection.json) as pickable rows for the first time, each carrying its `collectionSlug`.
2. For an already-on-disk collection, the existing 'Refresh from Nexus' action applies as scoped earlier (manual, backed-up, warns for Workshop rows).
3. For a genuinely NEW Workshop-only row (no local collection.json yet at all — nothing to scan against), the flow is necessarily 'fetch from Nexus first, THEN scan' rather than 'scan, then optionally refresh' — check whether the existing Step 1 → Step 2 picker flow needs a small branch for this case (fetch-then-continue) or whether it's simplest to just require a fetch before that row becomes scannable at all. Flag this as a judgment call if the UI flow isn't obvious rather than guessing silently — a small mockup addendum may be warranted given this changes the picker's own basic behavior, not just adding a button.
4. Same 'Vortex must be closed' precondition this app already requires everywhere a live DB read happens — confirm whether that's already enforced for this whole area or needs adding.

items.title: Missing-file list shows garbled slashes instead of real filenames for some mods
items.why: The expanded 'missing files' list for at least one mod (Dragon Voiced Word Walls, 63 missing) shows a string of stray slashes instead of readable filenames — this worked before the recent Extract fix, so it's likely a regression in how destination paths get computed for this mod's archive structure.
items.prompt:
MANDATORY LIVE DEBUGGING against the director's real data — do not guess. Real repro: 'Dragon Voiced Word Walls' (collection 'GTS Audio Overhaul - Resurrected') shows '63 missing' but the expanded file list renders as a long run of stray '/' characters joined by commas, not real filenames — screenshot confirms. This worked correctly before the recent Extract-fix commit (source/destination split); the director confirmed it 'were there originally, but now gone'.

GROUNDING: `web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`'s `rmfBuildMissingCell` (~line 234-253) already correctly maps `row.missing` entries via `.destination` for display — that code itself looks right. This strongly suggests the actual `destination` STRINGS being computed for this specific mod's files are themselves broken (each one reducing to just '/' or a near-empty fragment), not a display bug — i.e. the bug is upstream, in `lib/missing-files-scan.js`'s `resolveExpectedDestinations` / `lib/simple-installer.js`'s `resolveSimpleInstall` (or `resolveChoices` if this mod has recorded FOMOD choices — check `mod.choices?.type` first to know which path applies).

INVESTIGATE LIVE using the director's real collection/archive for this exact mod:
1. Find 'Dragon Voiced Word Walls' in the real 'GTS Audio Overhaul - Resurrected' collection.json, get its `mod.source` and `mod.choices`.
2. `listArchive` its real archive, dump the raw entries (paths) to see the actual structure — is this an unusually deep/flat/oddly-named archive that could trip up `findPathPrefix`'s stop-pattern matching?
3. Run `resolveExpectedDestinations` (or `resolveSimpleInstall`/`resolveChoices` directly, whichever path applies) against the real data and print the actual computed `{source, destination}` pairs — confirm whether `destination` really is coming out as just '/' or similar garbage for these files.
4. If confirmed: find WHY. Candidate causes to check, don't assume which without verifying: (a) the detected mod-root prefix ends up being almost the ENTIRE path for this mod's files (a stop-pattern match landing very late in the path for some structural reason specific to this archive), (b) a path-separator inconsistency (archive entries using '/' vs '\\' inconsistently) confusing the prefix-strip math, (c) something specific to this mod having recorded FOMOD choices that `resolveChoices` mishandles differently than `resolveSimpleInstall` does.

FIX the real, confirmed cause. Given this apparently regressed with the recent source/destination-split commit, also diff that commit's own changes to `resolveExpectedDestinations` against what it looked like before, in case the regression is literally in that refactor rather than a pre-existing latent bug newly exposed by the display fix.

VERIFY: re-run the real scan for this collection, confirm 'Dragon Voiced Word Walls' shows real, readable filenames in its missing-file list, not garbled slashes. Spot-check a couple of the OTHER currently-good-looking mods too, to make sure the fix doesn't disturb them. Handoff with what the real archive structure/computed paths actually looked like — don't report fixed without showing the real before/after data.

items.title: Clear stale end-of-flow banner on Preview re-arm
items.prompt: In Update Collection: re-doing Apply Ignores via Preview doesn't clear the stale end-of-flow completion banner until Apply re-succeeds. Wire callout-clearing into the Preview re-arm so the banner clears the moment the step is re-armed. Pre-existing minor issue; not blocking.
